habitat: Singly in open woodland, mixed bushveld, cattle kraals and rural suburbia. It runs briskly, stands upright and flicks one or both wings open.
summary: A common resident. Dark grey-brown above and white below, with bold black facial markings and spots. The bill is black above and orange below, and the legs are pale orange. In flight the wings are chestnut. The call is lip-sitsirupa, and the song is brisk and varied. The page uses Psophocichla litsitsirupa. This list keeps Turdus litsitsirupa. The Kemp name Groundscraper Thrush and the code RB were left unchanged.

head.pattern: Bold black facial markings. Dark grey-brown above.

viewNotes.note: Grey-brown above, white and boldly spotted below, standing upright.
Bold black facial markings. The bill is black above and orange below.
The underside in flight is not described.
Dark grey-brown above, without white wing spots.

calls.description: The call is 'lip-sitsirupa'. The song is brisk and melodious, with continually varied phrases. A grade A call from Ethiopia is named as a thrush-pipit and was not used. The selected file is a grade A song from Kruger, near Sabie Park. The filename is XC1188517-260129-073202_Tr1-Groundscraper-thrush-Nkorho-Bush-Lodge.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The page uses Psophocichla litsitsirupa. Dark grey-brown is not stored as one back colour. The legs are pale orange. A grade A Ethiopia file is named as a thrush-pipit and was not used. The selected recording is a grade A song from Kruger, and the recordist is given only as JJSUN. The Kemp code RB was left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^13=8192 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 4096–16384.
